Q1: Pentylcyclohexane exhibits known and significant hazards for environmental and oral exposures (Tier 1). Potential dermal and eye hazards are identified through an expanded perspective (Tier 2), while endocrine disruption hazards are assessed as low to moderate (Tier 3). However, there are significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards, as well as for inhalation and organ/systemic hazards, indicating that confident hazard assessments cannot be made in these areas.
Q2: Pentylcyclohexane is not currently found on any specified "Lists of Concern." This absence, coupled with several data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard categories, suggests that the chemical may not have been extensively studied, leading to an incomplete hazard assessment rather than confirmed safety.
Q3: While Pentylcyclohexane has a well-defined molecular formula (C11H22) and is categorized as a "Small Molecule" rather than an incompletely defined substance, its characterization is not exhaustive. With 392 literature references, it falls below the median for similar chemicals, and critically, three out of seven hazard categories (Carcinogenicity, Mutagenicity, Reproductive Hazards; Inhalation; and Organ and Systemic Hazards) are classified as data-deficient (Tier 4), indicating significant gaps in its hazard profile.
